name: Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe Châteauneuf-du-Pape La Crau 2019
text:
## Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe Châteauneuf-du-Pape La Crau 2019 (magnum)

**The story.** Vieux Télégraphe is one of the best-known names in [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC). Hippolyte Brunier founded it in 1898, when only one hectare was vines; the rest grew fruit and vegetables, which paid better than wine in those days. The first vintage bottled here was 1900. Henri Brunier expanded the vineyards and took the name abroad from the late 1940s, and his sons Frédéric and Daniel have run it since 1988. With 60.5 hectares it is one of the largest landholders in the appellation ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/vieux-telegraph-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine)).

The name comes from an old signal tower built in 1792 for [Claude Chappe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Chappe)'s optical telegraph, whose engraving still appears on the label ([Vieux Télégraphe](https://www.vieux-telegraphe.fr/categorie/infos-millesimes/vieux-telegraphe-millesimes/rouge/2019/), in French). Chappe's system was a chain of towers with pivoting wooden arms, each passing semaphore messages to the next by telescope, "the first practical telecommunications system of the industrial age", in use until the electric telegraph replaced it in the 1850s ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Chappe)).

**The vineyard: La Crau.** Vieux Télégraphe comes from the estate's oldest vines on the [La Crau](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+du+Vieux+T%C3%A9l%C3%A9graphe,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) plateau, one of the largest contiguous holdings there, where the surface is nothing but stones and pebbles over red clay and sand ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/vieux-telegraph-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine)). Wine Access describes 60-year-old vines pushing through layers of round, heavy [galets roulés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galets_roul%C3%A9s) to reach the red clay beneath ([Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2019-domaine-du-vieux-telegraphe-la-crau-chateauneuf-du-pape_4c894733-1ef5-40a3-b67f-3f5b06e544e3)). The usual blend is about 65% [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), 15% [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), 10% [Cinsault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinsaut) and 10% [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah). The grapes are mostly destemmed, fermented in oak vats, then aged nine months in concrete and the rest of the time in large 70-hectolitre foudres. Leve says it is usually better after 4 to 6 years in bottle, and the best vintages should be drunk 8 to 25 years after the harvest ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/vieux-telegraph-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine)). Your bottle is a magnum.

**The vintage.** 2019 was a scorching, drought year across the southern Rhône ([2019 European heatwaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_European_heatwaves)). The appellation's own [vintage report](https://ogi.chateauneuf.com/upload/files/Cha%CC%82teauneuf%20du%20Pape%202019%20%28Anglais%29.pdf) counts just 158 mm of rain over the growing season and a heat wave that peaked at 44.3°C on 28 June; the berries stayed small and thick-skinned, and rain on 18 September let the Grenache finish ripening. [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) says the reds are powerful, with more tannin than usual, surprisingly fresh acidity and warming alcohol, and that most will improve with age.

**What the critics say for 2019.** As collected on the [estate's 2019 page](https://www.vieux-telegraphe.fr/categorie/infos-millesimes/vieux-telegraphe-millesimes/rouge/2019/) and by [Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2019-domaine-du-vieux-telegraphe-la-crau-chateauneuf-du-pape_4c894733-1ef5-40a3-b67f-3f5b06e544e3):
- **Bettane + Desseauve: 98** (2022 guide). "The great emotion of our tasting": breathtaking finesse of texture and perfectly ripe fruit, with "the obviousness of great wine". "The cru is at the top of its art."
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 97** (Stuart Pigott, March 2022). "If anyone tells you that Châteauneuf is just a big red that's never elegant, then they need to taste this masterpiece of elegance." Joyful and serious, with "decades of aging potential".
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 96 to 98** (from barrel, October 2020). Smoky red and black fruit, crushed rocks, peppery [garrigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrigue) and truffly earth; full-bodied, tight and compact, with terrific mid-palate depth. Needs 5 to 7 years in bottle and will live for 30-plus.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 96+**. "A hugely successful vintage": sun-warmed stones, garrigue, black cherries and black olives; full-bodied, rich and velvety, with tremendous length and softly dusty tannins for "a long, positive evolution".
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 95** (Josh Raynolds, August 2021). Red and blue fruit liqueur, licorice, pipe tobacco and herbs; lush and weighty yet energetic, with velvety tannins.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 93** (James Molesworth, January 2022). "Silky and refined": cherry purée, plum reduction and raspberry coulis with rose petal, warm stone and lavender. Drink now to 2036. It also made Wine Spectator's Top 100 of 2022.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.9** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is seven years old, in magnum. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2026 to 2039, and Dunnuck wanted 5 to 7 years in bottle. The magnum is just opening its window and will improve for many years. If you open it now, decant two to three hours ahead; ideally save it for a big occasion in the early 2030s.

**Serving and food.** Serve at about 16 to 17°C. The Wine Cellar Insider suggests classic meat dishes, from veal and lamb to game, stews, barbecue and [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet), and even hearty fish like tuna. A magnum is made for a feast: a slow-roasted leg of lamb, a Provençal [daube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daube), or roast duck with olives.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Vieux Télégraphe at the moment; it turns up with merchants and at auction.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k); "Châteauneuf-du-Pape" means "the Pope's new castle" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **More than the whole north.** Châteauneuf's 3,200 hectares produce more wine than all of the northern Rhône ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **Vegetables before vines.** At the founding, fruit and vegetables paid better than wine, so only one hectare was planted with vines ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/vieux-telegraph-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine)).
- **"Ça grenache grave!"** The estate quotes Édouard Brunier's description of the 2019, untranslatable slang for something like "This is seriously Grenache!" ([Vieux Télégraphe](https://www.vieux-telegraphe.fr/categorie/infos-millesimes/vieux-telegraphe-millesimes/rouge/2019/)).
- **A Gigondas partnership.** The Bruniers also own Domaine Les Pallières in Gigondas, together with the American importer [Kermit Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermit_Lynch) ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/vieux-telegraph-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine)).
